docs.title: filings-rfb
docs.text:
Typed pandas readers for the Receita Federal do Brasil (RFB) CNPJ open data: Empresas, Estabelecimentos, Socios, Simples and the six lookup tables, read as memory-flat chunks.

Unofficial, community library. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the Receita Federal do Brasil; the emblem belongs to that agency.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text: Section Description Usage Installation, imports, and usage examples Examples Task-oriented recipes per reader API Reference Module-level functions and public interface FAQ Common questions

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
pip install filings-rfb

Until the first PyPI release is published, install from source: pip install git+https://github.com/guilhermegor/filings-rfb.git.

from filings_rfb import read_companies

for df_chunk in read_companies("2026-10"):
    ...

The RFB publishes one folder per month. Estabelecimentos (up to 2.3 GB per compressed part) and Simples (~3.2 GB inflated) are large: the readers stream them to disk and yield chunks.

docs.title: Feat
docs.text:
• read the RFB CNPJ lookup tables (read_lookup, CNPJ_LOOKUP_NAMES)
  • read Empresas (read_companies) and export it to Parquet (export_companies_parquet)
  • read Estabelecimentos with full CNPJ assembly (read_establishments)
  • read Socios with qualification codes and masked documents (read_partners)
  • read Simples, the Simples Nacional and MEI options (read_simples)
  • shared multi-part chunked iterator, resumable streaming downloader and RFB share catalogue

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Everything you need to develop, test, and release this library.

See also: Usage · API Reference · the repository's root CONTRIBUTING.md holds the authoritative branch/PR and commit-message policy.

docs.title: Setting up for development
docs.text:
The project ships both a Makefile and a parallel tasks.sh, so use whichever suits your machine — bash bin/venv.sh.

bash bin/venv.sh        # create the Poetry venv + install deps
bash bin/ensure_env.sh  # seed .env from .env.example
bash bin/precommit.sh   # install the git hooks

init composes ensure_env (seed .env), venv (create the Poetry virtualenv, install all dependencies including dev + docs), and precommit (install the git hooks). Poetry is auto-installed if missing.

docs.title: Tests and linting
docs.text:
poe unit_tests          # poetry run pytest tests/unit/
poe integration_tests   # poetry run pytest tests/integration/
poe lint                # ruff + mypy + codespell + pydocstyle + shell/sql/yaml gates

CI runs the same gates on every pull request; keep them green locally before pushing.

The bin/ scripts need bash 4 or later (they use associative arrays, declare -A). macOS ships bash 3.2 as /bin/bash, so on a Mac run brew install bash and put Homebrew's bin first on PATH; the macOS CI jobs do the same before running the tests.

docs.title: Verifying the built package
docs.text:
Before opening a release PR, confirm the wheel actually builds and imports — this catches packaging mistakes (a missing __init__, an unshipped _internal/ subpackage) that source-tree tests never surface:

poe install_dist_locally    # python -m build → install → smoke-import → report the built wheel

docs.title: Publishing the documentation (versioned, via mike)
docs.text:
The published site is versioned: a consumer pinned to an older release reads that release's docs, not HEAD. mike maintains the version tree on the gh-pages branch and MkDocs-Material renders the version dropdown.

Two workflows split the work:

Workflow Trigger What it does Docs - Strict Build Check (docs.yaml) every push + PR mkdocs build --strict only — catches broken links/nav before a release. Never deploys. Release to PyPI (release-pypi.yaml) manual release after the PyPI publish succeeds, deploys the released version with mike deploy --update-aliases <X.Y> latest

Because the deploy runs after publishing, the site only ever advertises versions that actually shipped. Notes:

  • Granularity is X.Y — 1.4.2 and 1.4.7 share the 1.4 entry; the latest alias always tracks the newest release and is the default landing version.
  • Prereleases never move latest — a version with a suffix (1.2.3rc1) builds and publishes, but the docs deploy job is skipped.

docs.title: One-time Pages setup
docs.text:
mike serves from the gh-pages branch, so Pages must be set to Deploy from a branch → gh-pages. The workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN cannot change that (it is a GitHub App token without repo-admin rights), so do it with your own gh auth:

poe enable_pages

This already runs inside poe init (after bootstrap), and is idempotent and non-blocking — it warns and continues if gh is absent/unauthenticated, no remote resolves, or you are not a repo admin (a fork), so it never breaks init.

Ordering matters: the gh-pages branch does not exist until the first release deploy creates it. Until then enable_pages deliberately leaves Pages untouched (so the site is never pointed at an empty branch) and tells you to re-run it. So: cut the first release, then run poe enable_pages once. Manual alternative: Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: Deploy from a branch → gh-pages / /.

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
1. Open an issue first, from the repository's issue template, stating what should change, why, and the files it touches. Every branch and PR starts from one.
  2. Branch off the default branch as <type>/<issue-number>-<slug> (feat/42-…, fix/57-…). The branch-has-issue check requires an issue number in contributor branch names; release/, dependabot/, and renovate/ branches are exempt.
  3. Fill out the PR template completely, with Closes #<issue-number> in the body.
  4. Ensure the CI checks (tests, lint, docs build) pass — they are the merge gate.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
Releases are tag-driven and secret-free when the project is connected to a GitHub remote:

  • The version is the git tag (via poetry-dynamic-versioning); pyproject.toml carries the version for Commitizen. Bump it only as part of a release. Trigger a release from the Actions tab (Release to PyPI / Release to Test PyPI, workflow_dispatch with the version), or by pushing a vX.Y.Z tag.
  • The release workflow runs the full test suite as a hard gate, builds with python -m build, and publishes via OIDC trusted publishing (pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish) — no token secrets are needed. Register the pending publishers below; GitHub creates the release-pypi and release-test-pypi environments on the first run.
  • The changelog is regenerated from tags at release/build time (poe changelog locally); CI never commits CHANGELOG.md back to the protected default branch.

docs.title: Maintainer setup — trusted publisher (one time, before the first release)
docs.text:
Register a trusted publisher on both pypi.org and test.pypi.org. Every claim must match the workflow exactly or the upload fails with an opaque invalid-publisher:

Claim Value Owner / repository your GitHub <owner> / <repo> Workflow filename release-pypi.yaml (PyPI) / release-test-pypi.yaml (Test PyPI) Environment release-pypi / release-test-pypi PyPI Project Name must equal the distribution name (name in pyproject.toml)

The GitHub Release step exists only in release-pypi.yaml, not in the Test PyPI workflow, so a change there is never rehearsed; diff the two workflows when editing either.

For the very first upload the project does not exist yet — register a pending publisher at the account level (not under an existing project's settings). Publishing from a laptop instead of CI is the one case that still needs an API token; OIDC works only from GitHub Actions.

docs.title: Choosing publish targets
docs.text: The scaffold wires the release workflows for the official public registry (PyPI) and a staging registry (Test PyPI). To publish to a private / non-official source instead — a git source (pip install git+https://…), a private PEP 503 index, or (for ecosystems that support it) GitHub Packages — wire the consumer-side source in pyproject.toml with an explicit-priority guard against dependency confusion (poetry's priority = "explicit"; pip --index-url, never --extra-index-url).

docs.title: Branding the docs site
docs.text:
The scaffold ships a placeholder brand image at docs/assets/logo.png, wired as the header logo/favicon (theme.logo / theme.favicon in mkdocs.yml) and as the landing hero on docs/index.md. To brand your site:

  1. Replace docs/assets/logo.png with your own asset (keep the filename, or update the two mkdocs.yml paths and the <img> in docs/index.md).
  2. Tune size, position and border inline on the <img> — width="200" (scale), align="right" (position) and style="border-radius: 15px;" (rounded) — in docs/index.md.
  3. Set the header colour in docs/stylesheets/brand.css. It holds one --md-primary-fg-color per colour scheme, so the header can match the logo; here it is the Receita Federal emblem's navy.

docs.title: Repository protection & security (one-time, scripted)
docs.text:
poe init runs three admin-gated helpers. They are idempotent and non-blocking: without gh, without auth, without a GitHub remote, or without repo-admin rights they warn and skip, so init still completes for contributors and offline scaffolds. Re-run any of them alone later:

Target What it provisions poe enable_pages GitHub Pages source (gh-pages branch for versioned docs, else Actions) poe enable_repo_rules The pr-quality-gate branch ruleset + the merge settings the PR gate needs poe enable_security Private vulnerability reporting, Dependabot alerts, Dependabot security updates

docs.title: The pr-quality-gate ruleset
docs.text:
Applied to ~DEFAULT_BRANCH (that ref survives a branch rename), looked up by name so a re-run updates in place instead of creating a duplicate:

Rule Setting Why pull_request required_approving_review_count: 0 ⚠️ Must be 0. GitHub forbids approving your own PR, so any value ≥ 1 locks a solo maintainer out of merging their own work. Zero still forces every change through a PR — that is the real guardrail. pull_request required_review_thread_resolution: true Makes review comments binding: an unresolved thread blocks the merge instead of being decorative. code_scanning CodeQL, security high_or_higher, alerts errors Alerts stay at errors: errors_and_warnings/all start blocking merges on stylistic queries, duplicating ruff/mypy with noise. copilot_code_review review_on_push: true Its own rule type — not a pull_request parameter (that returns HTTP 422 and makes the feature look UI-only). non_fast_forward, deletion on No force-push, no branch deletion on the default branch. required_status_checks empty by default ⚠️ Deliberate. A required check whose name never reports blocks every PR forever. Populate REQUIRED_CHECKS in bin/enable_repo_rules.sh from a real PR — gh api repos/:owner/:repo/commits/<sha>/check-runs --jq ".check_runs[].name" — then re-run.

Deliberately not enabled: Require code quality results (subjective AI severity on the merge path — ruff, mypy and the bin/check_*.py gates already enforce quality deterministically) and Restrict code coverage (preview; the floor is single-sourced in .coveragerc fail_under).

docs.title: Automatic vs manual — the boundary is repo config vs account plan
docs.text:
Nothing here needs a click. Every repository setting above is scripted. What is not scriptable is your account's entitlement: the copilot_code_review rule only fires if the author has access to Copilot code review, and code review is not part of Copilot Free. Without a qualifying plan the rule sits correctly configured and inert — no review appears and nothing errors. That silence is the trap, because the ruleset JSON looks perfect either way.

Every other rule (PR required, CI green, CodeQL clean) works regardless of any Copilot plan, so the ruleset is worth applying unconditionally. Copilot Pro is free for verified students, teachers and popular-OSS maintainers.

Do not diagnose this with gh api user/copilot_billing → 404: that endpoint is for org/enterprise seat management and 404s for a personal account even when Copilot Free is active.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: SECURITY.md at the repo root is auto-detected by GitHub (no API call) and flips Security policy to Enabled; poe enable_security turns on the matching private-reporting intake plus Dependabot alerts and security updates. Ordinary version bumps are separate — see .github/dependabot.yml, which uses versioning-strategy: lockfile-only so it refreshes poetry.lock (keeping CI honest about what consumers install) without ever rewriting your pyproject ranges.

docs.title: Automated PR flow (the quality gate)
docs.text:
Every PR is classified by bin/pr_gate.py (workflow pr-gate.yaml), which labels it, posts one sticky comment with a per-axis status table, and hands the safe classes to GitHub's native auto-merge. Two rules are the whole design:

Classified by PATH, never by diff size. The dangerous change is semantic, not big: a one-character edit to a schema/contract constant is the smallest possible diff and the most dangerous — and every test still passes, because the tests assert the contract that was written. So size never decides eligibility; the changed paths do. (The one place size still matters — an XL diff is vetoed — is waived for a lockfile-only diff, whose line count tracks how many dependency hashes moved, not risk.)

Risk class Paths Auto-merge? src src/ ❌ defines what "passing" means tests tests/ ❌ defines what "passing" means other anything unmatched ❌ unknown = unsafe (default-deny) ci .github/, bin/, Makefile, tasks.sh, .pre-commit-config.yaml ✅ deps pyproject.toml, poetry.lock, requirements.txt ✅ (the test suite is the gate) docs docs/, mkdocs.yml, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, … ✅

Consent is opt-OUT. The safe classes auto-merge with no label; add do-not-merge to force a human merge. Native auto-merge bypasses nothing — GitHub holds the merge until every required check of the ruleset is green, so the gate only decides eligibility, never whether it passed.

Edit the risk table (the RISK_PATHS constant) in bin/pr_gate.py for your project's real layout.

docs.title: ⚠️ After changing gate policy, backfill the open PRs
docs.text:
The gate runs on pull_request events, so a PR that was already open when you change the policy (the classification/consent rules in pr_gate.py, or allow_auto_merge / delete_branch_on_merge) is never re-evaluated — it keeps the labels and auto-merge state it got under the old rules until some new event touches it. That is not a bug; the gate simply never ran again. So after merging a policy change, run the backfill:

gh workflow run pr-gate.yaml -f backfill=true   # re-evaluates every open PR
# for a Dependabot PR, `gh pr comment <n> --body "@dependabot rebase"` also works

docs.title: Bot-merged PRs and the reconciler
docs.text: A PR merged by native auto-merge (a bot action) does not close its linked issue and does not delete its branch, even with delete_branch_on_merge on — bot-performed actions are deliberately inert to prevent automation recursion. pr-reconcile.yaml fixes both: it closes the Closes #N issues and deletes the head branch of merged PRs. Its scheduled daily run is the actual fix — scheduled events are exempt from the "no new workflow runs" suppression that also swallows the fast pull_request: [closed] path for a bot merge. Latency is up to one day; that is the accepted cost of not needing a personal access token.

docs.title: The work-ledger gate
docs.text: bin/check_backlog_ledger.py (pre-commit + CI) fails a branch that touches src/ or CI paths but adds no .specs/backlog/<kebab>_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.md ledger with a - [ ] checklist — making the per-branch work-ledger convention structural instead of a thing you remember. Routine docs/deps/tests-only branches need none.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Task-oriented, self-contained snippets for common uses of this library. Each recipe stands alone — copy it and adjust.

See also: Usage for the basics · API Reference for every public symbol.

docs.title: Recipe: iterate Empresas without loading it all
docs.text:
Each chunk is a typed frame, so aggregate as you go and keep memory flat.

from decimal import Decimal

from filings_rfb import read_companies

decimal_total = Decimal(0)
for df_chunk in read_companies("2026-10"):
    decimal_total += sum(df_chunk["capital_social"].dropna(), Decimal(0))
print(decimal_total)

docs.title: Recipe: find invalid or inactive establishments
docs.text:
situacao_cadastral is 02 for ATIVA; 01 NULA, 03 SUSPENSA, 04 INAPTA and 08 BAIXADA are the non-active ones.

from filings_rfb import read_establishments

int_invalid = int_inactive = 0
for df_chunk in read_establishments("2026-10"):
    int_invalid += int((~df_chunk["cnpj_valido"]).sum())
    int_inactive += int((df_chunk["situacao_cadastral"] != "02").sum())
print(int_invalid, int_inactive)

docs.title: Recipe: export to Parquet and query it with DuckDB
docs.text:
Reading the ZIPs always decompresses everything once; lazy querying only pays off afterwards, against a columnar file. Export once, then let DuckDB (installed on your side, not a dependency of this library) scan it.

from pathlib import Path

import duckdb

from filings_rfb import export_companies_parquet

path_parquet = export_companies_parquet("2026-10", Path("empresas_2026-10.parquet"))
print(
    duckdb.sql(
        f"SELECT razao_social, capital_social FROM '{path_parquet}' "
        "ORDER BY capital_social DESC LIMIT 5"
    )
)

docs.title: Recipe: read partners with masked documents
docs.text:
Individuals' CPFs arrive masked by RFB (***240659**) and stay that way; never try to unmask them. Qualification codes are text and join to the Qualificacoes lookup.

import pandas as pd

from filings_rfb import read_partners

list_legal_entities = [
    df_chunk[df_chunk["tipo_socio"] == "1"] for df_chunk in read_partners("2026-10")
]
df_legal_entities = pd.concat(list_legal_entities, ignore_index=True)

docs.title: Recipe: read a CNPJ lookup table
docs.text:
Turn a downloaded lookup ZIP into a typed frame. The ETag comes from the share listing and is stamped on every row, so a stored table says which upstream version produced it.

from pathlib import Path

from filings_rfb import read_lookup


df_cnaes = read_lookup(
    "Cnaes",
    Path("Cnaes.zip"),
    "https://arquivos.receitafederal.gov.br/public.php/dav/files/<token>/2026-10/Cnaes.zip",
    '"17e2f9b2f51164f0e35a0e6011551c63"',
)
print(df_cnaes[["code", "description"]].head())

docs.title: Recipe: Simples Nacional and MEI options
docs.text:
Simples.zip inflates to ~3.2 GB, so it is read as chunks too. Options are nullable booleans (a blank flag is null) and the dates are real dates; an option with no exclusion recorded has a null end date (a scheduled future exclusion is not null, so the count below leaves it out). Reduce each chunk as it arrives (count, aggregate or write it out) rather than collecting the rows: the companies in the Simples alone run to millions.

from filings_rfb import read_simples

int_active = 0
for df_chunk in read_simples("2026-10"):
    series_active = (
        df_chunk["opcao_pelo_simples"].fillna(False)
        & df_chunk["data_exclusao_simples"].isna()
    )
    int_active += int(series_active.sum())
print(f"{int_active:,} companies opted into the Simples Nacional with no exclusion recorded")

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Answers to common questions about using and developing this library. Add project-specific entries as they come up in issues.

See also: Usage · Examples · Contributing.

docs.title: How do I install it?
docs.text:
pip install filings-rfb
pip install "filings-rfb[parquet]"   # optional Parquet export

Until the first PyPI release is published, install from source: pip install git+https://github.com/guilhermegor/filings-rfb.git.

docs.title: How do I add or update a dependency?
docs.text:
Use Poetry so the lock file stays authoritative:

poetry add <package>          # runtime dependency
poetry add --group dev <package>   # dev-only tool

Every package the code imports must be a direct dependency — never rely on it arriving transitively through another package.

docs.title: Which Python versions are supported?
docs.text: See the python = "..." constraint in pyproject.toml; CI runs the test matrix against each.

docs.title: How is the version determined?
docs.text: The version is the git tag (via poetry-dynamic-versioning); pyproject.toml carries the version for Commitizen (1.0.0 at the first release) but the built wheel takes the tag. Cut a release from the release workflow — see Contributing.

docs.title: What is the cnpj.tar.gz at the root of the RFB share, and does the library use it?
docs.text: No, the library ignores it. It is a 63,954,782,749-byte (59.6 GiB) gzip of a tar (probably a single gzip member), last modified 2026-01-28 and never refreshed since. It appears to hold only the nine monthly folders 2025-05 to 2026-01 (inferred from the gzip trailer and byte-range checks, not a full listing), and the sampled files are byte-identical to the per-month zips that remain on the share, so it adds no data, cannot back-fill anything before 2025-05, and is impractical to read selectively (a gzip stream offers no known seek points). Download the YYYY-MM/<file>.zip parts you need instead. The evidence is in .specs/features/cnpj-tarball/design.md.

docs.title: Incident Records
docs.text:
What broke in this project, and what changed so it cannot break that way again. This page keeps debugging knowledge inside the codebase instead of in git history and one person's memory — the knowledge a team already paid for once should not have to be paid for twice.

See also: Usage · Contributing · Changelog.

docs.title: Not an ADR, and not a lessons store
docs.text:
An ADR records a decision made before something went wrong. An incident record documents one made because something already did — different trigger, different audience. If this project adopts ADRs later, keep the two separate rather than merging them into one grab-bag.

This is also not a copy of a scaffolding tool's own "lessons learned" store. That kind of store answers "what should every future generated project inherit" — this page answers "what bit this codebase, and what did we do about it." Different audience, different lifetime.

docs.title: Published on purpose — redact before you write
docs.text: This page ships in the published docs site, same as Usage. An incident can carry production detail (a hostname, a query, a customer-facing symptom) that should not reach a public site — redact or generalize it before committing the entry, the way an external postmortem omits internal specifics. If this project's site is genuinely public and entries cannot stay redacted, exclude incidents.md via exclude_docs in mkdocs.yml — and remove its Incidents entry from nav in the same change, or mkdocs build --strict fails — instead of leaving it half-written.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Five fields, in this order. Keep each to a few sentences — the entry stops getting written the day it takes an hour to fill in.

  • Symptom — what was observed, not what was wrong.
  • How it was found — the tool, command, or accident that surfaced it; "we were careful" does not belong here.
  • Root cause — measured, not assumed.
  • The change — what now makes this class of failure impossible, or loud instead of silent.
  • How we'd know it regressed — the gate, test, or assertion that would catch it coming back.

docs.title: TEMPLATE — replace with this project's first real incident
docs.text: Delete this section once you have an entry of your own. It stays only so a reader can see what a filled-in entry looks like — an empty page teaches readers there is nothing to read here.

docs.title: 2026-08-16 — Reconfiguring the logger leaked a file handle every time
docs.text:
Symptom. logging.FileHandler objects accumulated across the process lifetime whenever the logger was reconfigured (e.g. rotating to a new dated log file). Harmless in a short-lived script; in a long-running service the leaked file descriptors build up.

How it was found. Not by the test suite — ResourceWarning is not shown by default in Python. It surfaced only when the suite ran with -W always, while measuring something unrelated. The defect was invisible by construction, not by anyone's oversight.

Root cause. The reconfiguration path called logger.handlers.clear() to detach the old handler before attaching a new one. Clearing the list drops the Python reference; it does not close the OS file descriptor, which stays open until garbage collection runs.

The change. Close every existing handler explicitly before detaching it, so the descriptor is released immediately instead of at GC time. One call site — handlers.clear() appeared exactly once in the whole codebase, so no sibling caller was left unfixed.

How we'd know it regressed. A test reconfigures the logger twice and asserts the first handler's .stream is None after the second call — close() sets that attribute the moment the descriptor is released, so the assertion does not depend on garbage-collection timing. ⚠️ Measured separately: promoting bare ResourceWarning to error: in pytest.ini does not catch this alone — it is raised from __del__, an unraisable context pytest downgrades to PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning, so both warning classes must be promoted together or the suite still passes over a real leak.

docs.text:
Examples for installing and using this library.

See also: API Reference

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install filings-rfb
pip install 'filings-rfb[parquet]'   # optional: Parquet export

Or with Poetry:

poetry add filings-rfb

Until the first PyPI release is published, install from source: pip install git+https://github.com/guilhermegor/filings-rfb.git.

docs.title: Basic usage
docs.text:
Every dataset reader (read_companies, read_establishments, read_partners, read_simples) takes a reference month (YYYY-MM) and yields typed chunks. read_lookup is the exception: it takes str_table, path_zip, str_url, str_etag and returns a single DataFrame.

from filings_rfb import read_partners

for df_chunk in read_partners("2026-10"):
    ...

read_establishments (up to 2.3 GB per compressed part) and read_simples (~3.2 GB inflated) are the heaviest; keep path_workdir= to resume instead of re-downloading.

docs.title: Cataloguing the RFB CNPJ share
docs.text:
The Receita Federal publishes the CNPJ open data as one folder per reference month (YYYY-MM) on a public WebDAV share. filings_rfb.ingestion.cnpj._share lists what is there, without authentication, so a reader never builds a URL by hand:

from filings_rfb.ingestion.cnpj._share import (
    file_url,
    latest_reference_month,
    list_files,
    list_reference_months,
)

list_reference_months()          # ['2023-05', ..., '2026-10']
str_month = latest_reference_month()

for cls_file in list_files(str_month):
    print(cls_file.str_name, cls_file.int_size, cls_file.str_etag, cls_file.dt_last_modified)

file_url(str_month, "Empresas0.zip")   # plain-GET download URL, no redirect
  • list_files returns one WebdavEntry per file: str_name, int_size (bytes), str_etag (as the server sends it, quotes included) and dt_last_modified (UTC).
  • Requesting a month the share does not publish raises ValueError; there is no silent fallback to another month.
  • Every listing is a live request, so it reflects what RFB publishes now. If RFB rotates the share, change SHARE_TOKEN in _share.py and nothing else.

docs.title: Reading Empresas
docs.text:
read_companies(str_month) yields one typed pandas.DataFrame per chunk of each of the ten Empresas0.zip .. Empresas9.zip parts, so a month that inflates to ~3 GB is never held in memory at once. Each ZIP is streamed to disk with the resumable downloader and its single member is read as a stream, never extracted.

from filings_rfb import read_companies

for df_chunk in read_companies("2026-10", int_chunk_rows=500_000):
    print(df_chunk[["cnpj_basico", "razao_social", "capital_social"]].head(1))
  • capital_social is parsed from decimal-comma text (120000000000,00) to an exact Decimal, never through a float, with no rounding.
  • Every row carries the provenance columns plus source_etag (the part's ETag) and part_index (0-9); all chunks of one call share one ingestion_run_id.
  • A part the share does not list raises FileNotFoundError before any download starts; it is never skipped.
  • Pass path_workdir= to keep the downloaded ZIPs (a rerun resumes from them); by default each ZIP is deleted once consumed.

docs.title: Exporting to Parquet
docs.text:
export_companies_parquet(str_month, path_dest) drains the same iterator into one Parquet file (capital_social stored as decimal128(38, 2)). It needs the optional extra, which pulls in pyarrow:

pip install 'filings-rfb[parquet]'

Without it the call raises an ImportError that names the extra. Querying the Parquet lazily (DuckDB, Polars scan_parquet) is up to you; see Examples.

⚠️ Do not read these files with Polars directly: it silently misparses the .zip and corrupts latin-1 text.

docs.title: Downloading multi-GB archives
docs.text:
The RFB CNPJ archives reach 2.3 GB each (Estabelecimentos0.zip), so they must never be held in memory. download_file_streaming writes the body to disk in fixed-size chunks and can resume an interrupted transfer:

from pathlib import Path

from filings_rfb._internal.utils.stream_downloader import download_file_streaming

path_zip, str_etag = download_file_streaming(
    "https://example.org/Estabelecimentos0.zip",
    Path("data/raw/Estabelecimentos0.zip"),
)
  • The body is streamed into <dest>.part; only after the byte count matches Content-Length is it renamed onto the destination, so the final path never holds a partial file.
  • The server ETag is stored next to the partial file (<dest>.part.etag). A retry, or a later call after a crash, continues with Range: bytes=<n>- and If-Range: <etag>. If the ETag changed, or the leftover has no recorded ETag, the download restarts from zero.
  • After the rename the ETag is recorded in <dest>.etag. Calling again for a destination that has that sidecar sends If-None-Match: a 304 returns the existing file untouched with the stored ETag; a 200 downloads and replaces it. With no sidecar the file is downloaded afresh. This is how a rerun over a kept path_workdir avoids re-downloading every part.
  • The returned str_etag (empty when the server sends none) is for provenance.
  • A body shorter than Content-Length raises OSError after the bounded retries, keeping the partial file for the next attempt; a response without Content-Length raises ValueError.
  • It shares the guards of http_downloader (http/https only, public hosts only, redirects refused, bounded retries). download_file there still buffers the whole body: use it only for small files.

docs.title: Publishing to PyPI
docs.text:
Two GitHub Actions workflows handle releases (present when the repo has a GitHub remote):

  • release-test-pypi.yaml — publish to Test PyPI first.
  • release-pypi.yaml — publish to PyPI and cut a GitHub release.

Trigger either from the Actions tab (workflow_dispatch) with the version to release. Both gate on the new version being greater than the latest already published, build with python -m build, and publish through OIDC trusted publishing. No token secrets are needed.

Register a pending trusted publisher once on each index:

  • pypi.org: workflow release-pypi.yaml, environment release-pypi.
  • test.pypi.org: workflow release-test-pypi.yaml, environment release-test-pypi.

GitHub creates the environments on the first run.

The docs site (https://guilhermegor.github.io/filings-rfb/) returns 404 until the first release-pypi.yaml run's deploy_docs job (mike) creates the gh-pages branch. After that, run poe enable_pages once.

docs.title: Growing this section
docs.text:
This is a directory, not a single page, on purpose. An API reference grows once per shipped unit, so a single api.md becomes the largest page in the repo; splitting it later is trivial effort but rots every published deep link — and permanently, once versioned docs are live, because /<version>/api/#anchor exists forever. The premium for starting as a directory is one extra file and one nav level, paid once.

When you add pages:

  • Group by the codebase's own top-level split — never invent a parallel taxonomy (e.g. one page per public module, mirroring the package's own split). A reader who knows the package can then guess the URL, and the docs cannot drift from a structure they mirror.
  • Depth follows count, not taste. The real axis picks the sections; volume alone decides whether a section needs a second level.
  • Prose shared by one group lives once on that group's page, not restated per item.
  • Register every new page in mkdocs.yml nav: in the same commit. MkDocs builds an unregistered page anyway — it just vanishes from navigation, which is how a page silently goes missing (and what the check_docs_sections.py gate exists to catch).

docs.title: read_companies(str_month, int_chunk_rows=500_000, path_workdir=None) -> Iterator[pd.DataFrame]
docs.text: Yields the Empresas rows of a reference month (YYYY-MM), one typed DataFrame per chunk of each part 0-9. capital_social is an exact Decimal. Raises FileNotFoundError when a part is not published.

docs.title: export_companies_parquet(str_month, path_dest, int_chunk_rows=500_000, path_workdir=None) -> Path
docs.text: Writes the same rows to one Parquet file. Requires the filings-rfb[parquet] extra and raises an ImportError naming it otherwise.

docs.title: read_establishments(str_month, int_chunk_rows=500_000, path_workdir=None) -> Iterator[pd.DataFrame]
docs.text: Yields the Estabelecimentos rows of a reference month (YYYY-MM), one typed DataFrame per chunk of each part 0-9. Adds cnpj_completo (basic + order + check digits) and cnpj_valido (check-digit validation, alphanumeric-aware). The three date columns are datetime.date, with 00000000 and empty as null; cnae_fiscal_secundaria stays comma-separated text. Raises FileNotFoundError when a part is not published.

docs.title: read_partners(str_month, int_chunk_rows=500_000, path_workdir=None) -> Iterator[pd.DataFrame]
docs.text: Yields the Socios rows of a reference month, one typed DataFrame per chunk of each part 0-9. documento_socio is verbatim (RFB pre-masks an individual's CPF as ***dddddd**; it is never unmasked). documento_representante is null where RFB published ***000000** (no representative). qualificacao_socio and qualificacao_representante are two-character text codes that join to the Qualificacoes lookup. data_entrada is a datetime.date (00000000 and blank are null; any other value that is not YYYYMMDD raises ValueError). Raises FileNotFoundError when a part is not published.

docs.title: Module: filings_rfb.ingestion.cnpj.lookups
docs.text: Reads the six RFB CNPJ lookup tables: Cnaes, Motivos, Municipios, Naturezas, Paises and Qualificacoes (the partner/representative qualification, i.e. role).

docs.title: CNPJ_LOOKUP_NAMES: tuple[str, ...]
docs.text: The six table names read_lookup accepts.

docs.title: read_lookup(str_table, path_zip, str_url, str_etag) -> pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Reads one downloaded lookup ZIP. The archive must hold exactly one file member, whatever its name; the member is a headerless, ;-separated, quoted latin-1 CSV of code;description.

Parameter Meaning str_table One of CNPJ_LOOKUP_NAMES path_zip The archive on disk str_url The URL it was fetched from (stamped as url) str_etag The share's ETag for it (stamped as source_etag)

Returns code and description as text (leading zeros are kept), followed by the provenance columns (url, updated_at, source_key, package_version, ingestion_run_id, content_hash) and source_etag.

Raises ValueError for an unknown table or an archive with zero or several file members, and ContractError for a row that is not exactly two fields.

docs.title: read_simples(str_month, int_chunk_rows=500_000, path_workdir=None) -> Iterator[pd.DataFrame]
docs.text: Yields the Simples rows (Simples Nacional and MEI options) of a reference month (YYYY-MM), one typed DataFrame per chunk. Simples.zip is one un-numbered archive, read through the same shared iterator as the numbered datasets (part_index is always 0). opcao_pelo_simples and opcao_pelo_mei are nullable booleans (S/N; blank is null; anything else raises ValueError); the four date columns are datetime.date, with the RFB's 00000000 sentinel and blanks read as null, and any other value that is not YYYYMMDD raising ValueError. Raises FileNotFoundError when Simples.zip is not published.

docs.title: Adding new modules
docs.text:
Place new modules under src/filings_rfb/. Export public symbols from src/filings_rfb/__init__.py (and its __all__) so callers can do:

from filings_rfb import read_companies

Follow the one-class-per-file convention: utility functions with no shared state belong at module level, not wrapped in a class.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text: Convention Rule Type hints Required on all public functions, including -> None return types Docstrings NumPy style; explain why, not what Variable names Type-prefixed (str_, list_, cls_, dict_, …) Testing pytest-style functions with fixtures; name as test_<unit>_<scenario>_<expected>
